stem: A 3-year-old is reviewed after a fall onto the mouth, and the oral surgery team documents an alveolar degloving injury. Which description best matches this term?

options.text: A tooth that has been knocked out completely
A laceration of the oral tissues
A fracture of the maxilla or mandible
Bruising confined to the hard palate

explanation: Mucosa removed off the alveolus is the correct description of alveolar degloving. This term refers to the mucosa being stripped from the alveolar bone, rather than a tooth avulsion, laceration, fracture, or bruising.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because this describes a tooth avulsion, not alveolar degloving
optionExplanations.B: Correct because alveolar degloving means the mucosa is removed from the alveolus
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a laceration is a tissue tear, not stripping of mucosa from bone
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because this describes a bony fracture, not a soft tissue degloving injury
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because bruising of the hard palate is a contusion, not degloving
